Inverse-square equilibrium on R with finite one-sided forces: must the increasing particle sequence be affine? Original note: https://arquivo.pt/wayback/20201231041612id_/https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~itai/equilibrium.pdf

Existing external publication by Alper Ferudun, Equilibria of Inverse-Square Repulsion on the Line Are Arithmetic Progressions, v1.0 (3October2026), unrefereed AI-assisted preprint; not Alec Kriebel authorship. Theorem1.2 proves every nontrivial set of distinct real particles with finite equal left/right inverse-power forces is b+hZ, h>0, for1<s<=2, including the full original inverse-square case. Local finiteness follows from finite force; no uniform gap bound or attained extremal gap is required. Indexed affine conclusion uses increasing enumeration. No principal-value/arbitrary-label/all-force-law claim.
